translationRepairs: Cui Yuan, styled Youyu, came from Wucheng in Beizhou and was the eighth-generation descendant of Cui Liang, who had served as Vice Director of the Left Department of the Secretariat under the Northern Wei.

尚書左仆射 is the left pushe of the Shangshu, the Department of State Affairs, not an office of the Secretariat.
Cui Yuan, styled Youyu, was a man of Wucheng in Beizhou, eighth-generation descendant of Cui Liang, Vice Director of the Left Department of the Secretariat of Later Wei.

Yang Guozhong held the Sword River commandery in absentia and brought Yuan in as left chief military administrator with charge of the rear headquarters.

劍南 is Jiannan, not Sword River, but 節度 is a circuit military commission, not a commandery; the replacement still called it a commandery.

攝冢宰 is acting zhongzai, the classical chief-minister office, not chief mourner.

When Emperor Xuanzong died and Emperor Suzong was gravely ill, an edict appointed Jinqing acting chief minister (zhongzai); he firmly declined, saying: "The late Emperor's testamentary edict states that the Emperor shall hold court after three days; consulting the precedents of our ancestors, there is no provision for a chief minister; following the testamentary edict, he should attend court.
冢宰 in 無冢宰之文 is the chief-minister office, not a chief mourner.
Several days later Emperor Daizong ascended; again he was ordered to act as chief mourner, and only after firmly declining was he released from the duty.
Several days later Emperor Daizong ascended; again he was ordered to act as chief minister (zhongzai), and only after firmly declining was he released from the duty.
